newsitem.title: USA: Defense official says closed base jobs not ensured.
newsitem.headline: Defense official says closed base jobs not ensured.

text.p: Deputy Defence Secretary John White said Thursday the Clinton administration never guaranteed that its effort to save jobs at an Air Force base in California and another in Texas would result in any certain numbers of jobs kept.

"No sir," Deputy Defence Secretary John White said when asked at a Senate hearing if the Clinton administration had guaranteed that a set number of jobs would be saved and kept at McClellan Air Force Base in California and Kelly Air Force Base in Texas.

President Clinton agreed to a new round of base closings in 1995, including closing Air Force maintenance depots at those two bases, only on condition that that work be turned over to private contractors to save jobs.
Republicans accused Clinton of taking the action to win votes in California and Texas for his re-election in 1996.

White told the Senate Armed Services readiness subcommittee hearing that he visited the bases after Clinton made his decision in 1995 and told workers that while the president hoped to save their jobs, there was no guarantee how many would keep them.

"We were very careful to say that while obviously it was our expectation that there was an opportunity here, we could not make any guarantees with respect to work after the period in which the transition (to private contractors) took place," White said.

Sen. Charles Robb, a Virginia Democrat who had asked about the guarantee, said "So the expectations of those communities would be based on optimism, hope, but no specific guarantee explicit or implicit?"
